thread:
maria: Quickstart bug: the Edge sample uses require() and throws in Vercel Edge runtime. Anyone seen this?

maria: Error is `SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module` when deploying the sample app from docs. Local Node (CJS) works fine. :thinking_face:

alex: That usually means the bundle ended up with ESM import syntax but runtime expects CJS, or vice versa. What does your package.json look like?

maria: package.json has no "type" field (default CJS). The docs example shows: `const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')` in examples. On Edge we should be using `import` though.

jordan: For the Edge runtime we ship an ESM build. In TS/ESM you should do: `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference/edge'` or `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference/edge'` depending on your bundler.

maria: I tried `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference/edge'` and got TS types complaining: "Module has no default export." :facepalm:

alex: That one is a typing/export shape issue. Our published package has `export =` in the CJS build and `export default` in the ESM build — historically we've tried to support both which causes confusion for TS consumers. Quick fixes:
1) `import Redwood = require('@redwood/inference')` in TS (if using --allowSyntheticDefaultImports false)
2) `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` usually works
3) set "esModuleInterop": true in tsconfig and use `import Redwood from ...`

maria: For the Edge sample (plain JS) what should the docs show so it works on Vercel Edge without readers stumbling over package.json tweaks?

olivia: Docs here — we should make the example match the runtime we're recommending. If we want Edge-first examples, show ESM `import` and note the `type: "module"` or runtime-specific bundler rule. I'll open a doc PR.

jordan: Also add a short note about named vs default export and a single one-line example for CommonJS:
```
// CommonJS
const { createClient } = require('@redwood/inference')

// ESM
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
```
That avoids default export headaches.

maria: FYI CI flagged a sample app test failing on the edge-smoke suite after I changed the quickstart to CJS. Posting the log:
```
/var/task/index.js:1
import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'
^^^^^^
SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
    at wrapSafe (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:992:16)
    at Module._compile (internal/modules/cjs/loader.js:1039:27)
```

ci-bot: edge-smoke (main) — build #482 failed: failing test `edge-quickstart-deploy` — https://ci.internal/build/482 :x:

alex: That log is Node trying to run an ESM file as CJS. If CI is running `node index.js` without `--experimental-modules` or without package.json `type: module`, you'll get that. If it's on Vercel Edge, their bundler expects ESM; for local CI we need to either transpile or run with node >=16 and type:module.

olivia: Action items: I'll update the Quickstart to show both variants (CJS + ESM) and add a short footnote about tsconfig/esModuleInterop. Also add a link to the Edge troubleshooting note.

jordan: We should also publish a tiny `edge` entrypoint that only exports ESM-friendly named exports to avoid default export confusion. Filing a tiny infra ticket for packaging.

maria: Thanks — will try the `import { createClient }` switch and report back. If docs change lands, that should reduce onboarding friction a lot. :thumbsup:

olivia: Thanks for the report, @maria. I'll tag you on the PR so you can confirm the examples reproduce in Vercel Edge and CI.

maria: Confirmed — `import { createClient } from '@redwood/inference'` + no package.json changes works in the Vercel Edge deploy. CI still needs adjustment.

ci-bot: edge-smoke (main) — build #483 started: running `edge-quickstart-deploy`

alex: For CI we can switch the smoke runner to build with esbuild and run the output, or set `type: module` in the sample app used by tests. I'll make a short PR for the runner config.

maria: Great, thanks. Happy to test the new docs once they're up.

olivia: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/212 — includes ESM/CJS side-by-side quickstart and troubleshooting notes. Please review. :sparkles:
